business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Advertising Media Arbitrage and Affiliate Lead Gen

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, heavily influenced by French and Belgian law; partnership law codified in the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (signed April 1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty of 23 August 2012
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty of 1 April 2018

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 May 2019 concerning the Register of Beneficial Owners; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 24 July 2015 on the Register of Commercial and Companies (LBR legal framework); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (for SCSp formation and UBO clauses).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Deed of Constitution (Acte de Constitution) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial act executed by a sworn civil-law notary; no Hague Apostille required for acts of Luxembourg notaries intended for Luxembourg authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-Opposition to Company Name (Certificat de non-opposition / Autorisation d'usage de dénomination sociale)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic administrative clearance issued electronically via LBR portal; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport or Government-Issued Identity Document of Each General Partner, Limited Partner, and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of country of issue (e.g., police authority, municipal registry, ministry of interior)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (5 October 1961) apostille from the country of origin, followed by certified translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Excerpt of Commercial Register (Registre de Commerce) of Any Foreign Corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial registry in the corporate partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is a Contracting State) or bilateral Consular Legalization at the competent consulate; certified French/German translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Address and Domiciliation for Registered Office (Certificat de Bureaux / Domiciliation Agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg domiciliation agent (PSF-branch) or landlord / real estate representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized lease or duly signed domiciliation agreement; non-Luxembourg supporting documents require Hague Apostille if issued abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference and Source of Funds Evidence for Initial Capital Contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank institution of the general partner or relevant third-party financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-stamped letters apostilled under the Hague Convention if issued by non-Luxembourg banks

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all partners, directors, intermediaries and UBOs against (i) the Luxembourg national consolidated list of asset-freeze measures (Ministry of Finance/CSSF), (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Reg. 269/2014 and EU Reg. 833/2014, as amended), (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, and (iv) the U.S. OFAC SDN List. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required under Article 2-3 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 for Politically Exposed Persons (foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, international organization PEPs), their family members and known close associates. Screening must cover the beneficial owners, the general partner, and any authorized representatives; results must be documented and retained for at least five years post business relationship termination. The SCSp's professional (PSF, notary, fiduciary, credit institution) must apply enhanced ongoing monitoring where a PEP or sanctions hit is detected, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification before any distribution or media-buying cash flow operation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-portal available at www.lbr.lu (RCSL registration module, formerly e-justice portal; filings also possible via www.myguichet.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name may be expressed in any language using the Latin alphabet but must be accompanied, wherever RCSL or notarial practice requires, by a transliteration and a compulsory French or German translation in the articles of association. Registration in the RCSL is bilingual (French/German) and the trade name must be distinguishable from all existing and pending names registered in Luxembourg. The name must not contravene Luxembourg public order, good morals, or international law protected designations, and must not mislead the public as to the company type; a translation must not contain varying meaning from the original.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK (requires prior authorization from the Minister of Finance and competent banking regulator CSSF under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector)
ASSURANCE / REASSURANCE / INSURANCE (requires pre-authorization from the Commissariat aux Assurances)
FIDUCIAIRE / TRUST (requires specific licensing and may be refused for pure media-buying entities)
PSF / PROFESSIONNEL DU SECTEUR FINANCIER (restricted to licensed financial-sector professionals)
SOGIÉTÉ D'INVESTISSEMENT / FONDS / UCITS / SIF / SICAV (reserved to undertakings authorized and supervised by the CSSF)
CABINET / AVOCAT / NOTAIRE / EXPERT-COMPTABLE (restricted to regulated liberal professions)
UNIVERSITY / UNIVERSITÉ / ÉCOLE / LYCEE (requires prior ministerial approval from the Ministry of Education)
LUXEMBOURG / LUXEMBURG (as part of the corporate name requires justification and prior authorization to prevent misleading association with national or public institutions)
COMMERCE / INDUSTRIE / NATIONAL / OFFICIEL (where the term falsely implies governmental status or national franchise)

HOLDING / FINANCIÈRE / PATRIMONIÈRE (sensitive: requires conformity with the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915, tax transparency requirements, and may be refused where the proposed activity, such as media buying, is inconsistent with the holding designation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notice from the RCSL/LBR Registrar. The applicant may within fifteen (15) working days from notification (i) file a formal written appeal with the Registrar containing corrected alternatives, or (ii) submit a motion in summary proceedings (référé) before the Luxembourg District Court commercial chamber (Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg, chambre commerciale) seeking annulment or amendment of the refusal. Concurrently, the applicant may reserve a modified name via the LBR portal, which triggers a fresh 90-day reservation window. Where the refusal is based on a protected token (e.g., 'bank' or 'fund'), the only appeal route is to obtain the relevant ministerial/CSSF prior authorization and re-submit the name together with that authorization. The RCSL must rule on the re-submission within one month. If the judicial appeal succeeds, the court issues an order allowing the name, and the applicant must complete RCSL registration of the SCSp within the remaining reservation period, failing which a new reservation fee and protocol applies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without physical presence is not acceptable for an SCSp exercising commercial activity in Luxembourg. Luxembourg law (Article 44 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; LBR registration requirements) requires an effective registered office in Luxembourg. However, domiciliation (home office) is permissible under strict conditions: the SCSp may use a domiciliation agreement provided by a licensed professional (a 'société de domiciliation' or a regulated PSF) at a physical address in Luxembourg where the statutory records, corporate books, and RCSL correspondence are kept. For an affiliate media-buying vehicle with no employees in Luxembourg, a licensed domiciliation agent is acceptable and common, provided the agent holds the required professional status and the arrangement is not used for artificial tax structuring that would trigger substance-over-form challenges under the OECD BEPS and EU ATAD standards. The degree of substance required remains minimal for an SCSp under Luxembourg administrative practice, but must include a registered address, a local general partner (legal or natural person), proper accounting records, and compliance with UBO registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-negligible, estimated at 10% per year for a small SCSp with no licensed financial activities; CSSF and RCSL conduct risk-based unannounced inspections primarily on regulated PSF providers and domiciliation agents. The unannounced inspection risk rises to 25-35% if the SCSp acts as a financial intermediary for payment flows, engages in high-volume media buying with third-party trust accounts, or lacks a professional local general partner. In all cases the domiciliation agent may be inspected annually by CSSF.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL/LBR name reservation and non-opposition certificate filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by LBR (currently EUR 19 electronic filing base plus registry processing fees; estimated at EUR 75-85 total; Hedged at USD 90)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the deed of constitution (Acte de Constitution) of the SCSp, including drafting by Luxembourg notary and translation attachments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Notary (Ministerial officer appointed by the Grand Duke)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff fixed by Grand-Ducal regulation on notarial fees (scale based on capital contribution table; typical minimum for SCSp baseline EUR 1,300-1,600 plus notary out-of-pocket costs)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign corporate and partner identity documents (per-document average over 6 required documents, including certified translations into French/German)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of document issue (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO) plus sworn translator registered in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of EUR 20-60 per apostille (statutory fee of issuing authority) plus EUR 40-80 per 100-word certified translation by a court-sworn Luxembourg translator

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR commercial register (RCSL) filing and publication of incorporation, including certified digital extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCSL operating under the Ministry of Justice; online filing via LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR fee schedule for electronic filing of a new commercial company dossier (estimated EUR 130-150; USD 160)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) registration and AML/CFT KYC compliance file assembly, PEP/sanctions screening of all partners and UBOs, and legal memorandum on beneficial ownership piecing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / registered AML professional operating under CSSF Regulation No 12-02
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an SCSp PE/affiliate structure: fixed legal fee of EUR 2,500-4,000 plus CSSF RBE e-filing fee (EUR 0-75), dependent on the number of intermediate holding layers present in the ownership chain

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation agreement for registered office with licensed domiciliation/PSF agent (annual, pre-incorporation first-year fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company or PSF
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for SCSp domiciliation: EUR 1,200-1,500 per annum for a standard holding/SCSp dossier (USD 1,600)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Part III, Articles 13-1 to 13-29 concerning the société en commandite spéciale); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 June 2018 relating to the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Extrait de l'acte de constitution et dépôt au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS incorporation filing and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum capital; capital is fixed freely in the partnership agreement. Contributions may be in cash, in kind or in industry, and no escrow or bank blocked account is required by Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE GENERAL PARTNER OF [SCSP], DATED [DATE]: The sole general partner, acting for the partnership, resolves that: (1) the subscription of partnership interests by the initial limited partner(s) identified in the contribution schedule is approved, and capital commitments shall be paid in accordance with that schedule; (2) the registered office of the SCSp is adopted at [address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed as manager and authorized to sole-sign for the SCSp; (4) the manager and external counsel are authorized to file this resolution and the partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), to effect the required publications and to complete all incorporation formalities. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare, execute and, if contractually required, notarize the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External notary (for authentic form) or legal counsel; RCS portal via LBR for subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement in English or French with express submission to Luxembourg law; set out the limited partner(s), general partner, capital commitments, profit-sharing, management powers, and dissolution events. If a notarial deed is required by the fund's constitutional documents, execute before a Luxembourg notary; otherwise execute by private writing. Where any partner is a non-resident entity, attach a certificate of legal existence and an incumbency certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of legal existence and incumbency for corporate partners
Passport or ID of natural person partners/managers
Proof of registered office availability (letter of consent from the address provider)
Clean criminal record certificate of the proposed manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the RCS pre-filing check identifies missing schedules, the document can be amended by private deed and re-signed; any delay is cured within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation documents with the RCS and obtain the registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online portal; publication in RESA by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the deposit request on the LBR portal (lbr.lu) using the authenticated space, attach the executed partnership agreement, the manager's appointment and acceptance, the registered office consent, and pay fees online. The RCS issues a certificate of registration and transmits the file for publication in RESA. The registration extract must be recovered before opening bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration/publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RCS may issue a formal notice to regularize within one month; if rejected for formal deficiency, the filing can be re-submitted after correction without losing priority if done within 15 days. An appeal from a refusal lies to the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Luxembourg VAT Administration and obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration application using the standard form 010/VAT or via the AEDT online portal. Since affiliate media buying is an advertising activity, VAT registration is required when the business is established in Luxembourg or supplies taxable services there; registration should also be requested for B2B cross-border services to facilitate reverse-charge compliance. Attach the RCS extract and proof of authorized signatory.
required_dossiers: Evidence of premises in Luxembourg (lease agreement)
Description of activities and projected turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests further information, provide supplementary business plan within 15 days; if a VAT ID is not issued, a new application can be made immediately after compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as an employer with the Luxembourg social security office, if engaging staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the employer registration form (certificat de registre patronal), submit the RCS extract and employment contracts or a hiring plan. Obtain an employer number for social security contributions. Register each employee for sickness, pension, and accident insurance, and enrol the company with the occupational health service where applicable.
required_dossiers: Copy of employment contracts / hiring plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS queries the nature of employment, provide amended contracts or a written explanation within 10 business days; no penalty is imposed if registration is perfected before the first salary payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the economic unit / statistical declaration and obtain a STATEC business number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: STATEC – Business Register (Registre statistique des entreprises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the single 'My Guichet' / RCS process, company data is automatically transmitted to STATEC. Confirm that the registered ISIC 7310 code has been correctly captured, and request a STATEC business number if required for statistical or environmental declarations. No separate industry licence is required for digital advertising.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If there is a mismatch in the NACE/ISIC code, file a declaration of modification with the RCS to amend the activity code, then notify STATEC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a corporate bank account and arrange payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed credit institution in Luxembourg or a recognized EU bank; no CSSF licence is required for the SCSp itself
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS extract, partnership agreement, proof of registered office, UBO declaration, business plan, and AML/CFT compliance forms. Because affiliate media buying is considered medium-risk, the bank may request source of funds, projected flows, counterparty lists, and client due diligence questionnaires. Set up ACH, wire transfer, and Wise payment rails in accordance with the bank's online banking policy.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of beneficial owners and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information, respond within the stated deadline; if rejected, approach an alternative bank with the full file, or seek a 'second opinion' mechanism only in narrow cases under applicable banking rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File beneficial ownership declaration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration through the LBR portal, identifying each limited partner holding more than 25% of interests or otherwise controlling the SCSp. Use the specific RBE electronic form. For an SCSp, the general partner and qualifying limited partners must be listed.
required_dossiers: List of beneficial owners with identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE queries the control percentage, provide an updated capital table or explanatory note; late filing may trigger criminal and civil penalties; corrections can be filed online without reopening the initial declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – office-based digital advertising; no industrial licensing board is involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating licence required for ISIC 7310 affiliate media buying.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D – Exempt (office activity; no full EIA report or registration required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – zero industrial discharge. Office wastewater is connected to municipal sewerage and must meet local discharge by-laws; waste handling must comply with Luxembourg waste-management regulations and ITM workplace guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must hold a valid fire safety compliance certificate issued by the Service d'Incendie et de Secours; structural load inspection certificate is required where the lease or building permit mandates it; workplace clearance from the Luxembourg Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) must cover electrical safety, lighting, ventilation, health, and ergonomic standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Primary portals: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.public.lu; VAT and customs filing via the eCDF electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An SCSp is a fiscally transparent special limited partnership and is not itself subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax. For formal tax identity, the entity must first be registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) and obtain its RCS/matricule number. The Luxembourg VAT identification number is then obtained separately from the AEDT VAT administration, normally via the MyGuichet and eCDF online procedures. A foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment may register directly for VAT or appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative. A national TIN is not allocated to the transparent SCSp itself for direct tax purposes; tax identity flows through to the partners. In practice, the operative statutory identifiers for the SCSp are the RCS registration number and the Luxembourg VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. The tax classification of an SCSp follows legal-form analysis and is transparent by default. There is no voluntary partnership election available to convert the SCSp into a corporation. Where hybrid entities or hybrid instruments are involved, the Luxembourg ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules can override the default transparency to recharacterise income or deny deductions in order to prevent double non-taxation. A fully taxable vehicle such as a SOPARFI may be chosen instead as a structuring alternative, but that is a commercial incorporation choice rather than a tax classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg imposes no general monetary VAT-registration threshold for Luxembourg-established taxable persons. The EU Union One-Stop-Shop threshold of EUR 10,000 applies to intra-EU distance sales of goods and electronically supplied cross-border services. Resident small businesses with annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 may qualify for the small-business VAT exemption. For the SCSp affiliate media-buying activity, VAT registration is required before making taxable supplies in Luxembourg where such supplies are not outside the scope under B2B place-of-supply rules or reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate general B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance. There is no central financial clearance API and no digital stamping requirement for commercial invoices. Invoices to Luxembourg public-sector entities must, however, be submitted in structured PEPPOL format pursuant to the Luxembourg B2G e-invoicing mandate in force since 2020. VAT returns, export declarations and related periodic filings are submitted through the AEDT eCDF portal. Electronic invoices in other formats are permitted provided they comply with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and Luxembourg record-keeping requirements. The statutory retention period for invoices is 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Luxembourg applies 0% VAT to exports of goods where the supplier proves that the goods physically leave the EU under a valid customs export declaration and that title and control have passed to a buyer established outside Luxembourg. For the ISIC 7310 affiliate media-buying activity, zero-rating is not the normal mechanism. B2B advertising and performance-marketing services supplied to a foreign taxable customer are outside Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule and should be evidenced by the customer's foreign VAT registration or equivalent foreign business evidence and by a properly addressed commercial contract. B2C digital advertising and lead-generation services supplied to non-Luxembourg consumers may remain taxable in Luxembourg unless an exemption applies. A legitimate zero-rating claim therefore applies mainly to physically exported goods or qualifying export-related services, all supported by proof of dispatch, transport, export customs declaration and transfer of ownership.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Luxembourg eCDF/NCTS electronic customs channel and any required export licences
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from the EU to the contractually designated destination
Commercial invoice, purchase order, signed sales contract and documentary proof of transfer of ownership and risk to the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement showing receipt of payment from the non-resident counterparty
Foreign customer VAT identification number or equivalent overseas business-status evidence where the export or outside-Luxembourg treatment is based on the customer's taxable-person status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg does not impose exchange-control repatriation as a legal condition for VAT export treatment, but this compliance dossier applies a 180-day inward-remittance documentation deadline. If missing or defective, the AEDT can retrospectively disallow zero-rating, redetermine Luxembourg VAT on the full value of the affected supply, and recover the unpaid VAT together with default interest. Fraudulent or intentionally misleading export-zero-rating claims are subject to Luxembourg statutory penalty tax, administrative fines and possible referral to the criminal tax prosecutor. Participants in VAT-fraud chains may also face joint and several personal liability. All documentation supporting export or outside-scope treatment must be retained for 10 years from the invoice date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, AML/KYC supervisory matters, and payment system oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility and unrestricted capital movement apply under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Luxembourg maintains no exchange control regime, no capital account restrictions, and no separate formalities for profit remittance or transfer of funds. Banks apply standard anti-money laundering and sanctions screening only, in accordance with CSSF Circulars and Luxembourg law, not exchange-control permits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts or any other foreign currency proceeds. Foreign currency may be retained freely or converted at market rates without obligation to sell to the central bank or a licensed intermediary.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium under strictly regulated conditions. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) holding a passport into Luxembourg or a licence issued by an EEA authority can provide payment accounts to an SCSp, but many reject high-velocity affiliate-media flows unless a complete documentary trail is provided. Offshore and non-EEA digital EMI platforms not licensed or passported into Luxembourg should be considered legally non-viable as primary banking rails; they may be used at most for ancillary treasury purposes if they hold an EU payment institution licence and maintain client segregation, but never as the sole clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence or an equivalent e-identity verification interview is generally mandatory for a newly established non-resident SCSp. Remote opening is permitted only on a case-by-case basis using secure video identification, and it almost always requires certified constitutional documents, notarized or apostilled passports, evidence of registered office in Luxembourg, satisfaction of enhanced due diligence, and confirmation of the identity and authority of the general partner. The ultimate beneficial owners and authorised signatories must expect direct contact from Luxembourg compliance officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SCSp with no operating history, no audited financial statements, and no measurable commercial track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement (contrat de société), current RCSL registration extract, registered office certificate, UBO declaration, partners' resolutions, detailed business plan covering the affiliate media-buying model, executed contracts with major demand partners and publishers, projected cash projections, parent-company bank references, and tax or VAT registration confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border payments to affiliate networks, publisher accounts, or media buying platforms in multiple jurisdictions including higher-risk states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying commercial contract dossier: insertion orders, programmatic advertising platform statements, publisher payout reports, affiliate network settlement details, invoice reconciliation reports, lead or click-volume documentation, complete beneficiary payment list, sanctions and PEP screening results, and a written narrative describing the end-to-end money flow with supporting transaction tracking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp structure with zero mandatory capital and limited-partner participation that could resemble unregulated collective investment activity, money laundering, or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel confirming the SCSp is a commercial partnership and not an undertaking for collective investment; tax residency certificate; capital call and distribution resolutions; economic substance documentation; full identity and address disclosure of all partners; partnership bank statements evidencing real treasury activity; and documented justification for each distribution and return of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain involving a foreign corporate general partner or a multi-tieratedholding structure that hampers transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register extracts, corporate registry records from each intermediate jurisdiction, an organisational structure chart, passports or national identity cards of ultimate owners, corporate constitutional documents, notarized registration certificates, professional references from an existing banking institution, and a signed compliance declaration accepting Luxembourg AML/KYC duties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from a non-resident affiliate must be routed using SWIFT MT103 or MT202/MT202COV wire transfers to the SCSp's account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance instruction should cite the Eurosystem balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment equity or other capital, typically reported under 'Direct Investment: Equity Capital' or a comparable code accepted by the BCL; the customer must provide the bank with a capital call notice, partner resolution, executed partnership agreement, and a source-of-wealth declaration. Beneficiary naming must correspond exactly to the SCSp legal name and bank account to ensure straight-through processing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfers are the primary clearing rail for euro-denominated affiliate and publisher payouts within the EEA. For non-EEA destinations, SWIFT MT103 is the standard commercial wire mechanism, with beneficiary BIC/IBAN or ABA/account details as required. Commercial letters of credit are not suitable for performance-based media-buying open-account settlements and should be avoided; documentary trade instruments are used only if a particular publisher contract demands them. All outbound disbursements must reference the applicable invoice number, campaign identifier, purchase order, or publisher settlement statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot and outright forward contracts with a Luxembourg/EEA licensed credit institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without deliverable onshore markets, subject to bank counterparty policy and internal risk approval
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for longer-term EUR/USD and EUR/GBP balance-sheet hedging
Plain-vanilla FX options (European puts and calls) used to hedge identified commercial media-buying currency exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, no later than one month after the anniversary of the initial filing or within one month of any change to beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019; repeated non-compliance may trigger criminal penalties and removal of general partner or manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership information return (combined corporate income tax and municipal business tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SCSp, the return is due by 31 December of the following year; if fiscal year varies, within six months of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-file penalties typically 10% of the assessed tax; continuous default may result in a lien, forced administrative assessment, and a fine of up to EUR 25,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the RCS (only if the SCSp does not qualify for the small-partnership exemption)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 500 to EUR 2,000; failure to file suppresses evidence in litigation and can lead to strike-off of the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total over EUR 4,400,000; net turnover over EUR 8,800,000; average staff above 50. SCSp entities generally qualify for the small-entity exemption when the general partner is an individual or a permitted qualifying unlimited-liability partner.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002) or IFRS if voluntarily adopted; financial statements for SCSp are typically not required for publication if the partnership is under the statutory small-partnership exemption.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually confirm the accuracy of the beneficial ownership data filed in the RBE; in addition, any transfer of limited partnership interests must be recorded in the RBE within one month. The general partner must update the internal register of partners upon every transfer and confirm the conformity of the RBE data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (kept on-site, not filed unless requested)
Fixed asset register and accounting books (if required)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 4,000 (typical Luxembourg domiciliation and corporate agent annual fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 20,000 (if statutory audit is triggered; small SCSp normally exempt)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: SCSp is fiscally transparent (pass-through); no entity-level corporate income tax. Aggregated Luxembourg headline CIT rate for corporate partners: 24.94% (CIT 17.00% + solidarity surcharge 1.19% + municipal business tax 6.75% in Luxembourg City).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg IP Box 80% exemption on qualifying IP royalty income (effective rate ~4.99%); participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains under LIR Art. 147); notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity; as a partnership, SCSp is exempt from Luxembourg net wealth tax and corporate minimum tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward for losses incurred as from tax year 2017 (pre-2017 losses expire after 17 years); annual imputation is unrestricted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ACD Form 200 - Declaration for corporate income tax (Formulaire pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) with SCSp income-allocation annexes; filed electronically through the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) e-filing service on MyGuichet.lu (business space) / MyDTD portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 May of the following year on paper; electronic filing automatically extends the deadline to 31 December of the following year. An SCSp is also obliged to report annually to the RCS (annual accounts/listing) within 7-11 months of year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, RCS Luxembourg trade register number, corporate identification number, fiscal year dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp having no Luxembourg office must still obtain an RCS corporate file and appoint an authorised local agent; the tax file must state Luxembourg partner share percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre A - Identification and exercising period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period and confirmation that the period does not exceed 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be individually named, with their residence state, tax identification number and proportional share of profit applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B - Commercial result and turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net worldwide profit of the partnership (media-buying commissions, lead-generation revenue) before partner allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp reports total profit as an informational aggregation; the attribution to each partner is computable per the partnership agreement, and the ACD taxes only the Luxembourg-resident and Luxembourg-source portions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre C - Non-deductible and add-back items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, partially non-deductible entertainment, excessive management fees) and declaration of losses carried forward taken into account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, only expenses effectively linked to Luxembourg-source income may be deducted; add-backs must be allocated in the same ratio as profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre E - Financial and exceptional items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, withholding tax credits, dividends and capital gains declared separately; used for the participation exemption, net wealth and interest deduction reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners claiming double-tax relief must attach a schedule of taxes withheld at source and the relevant DTA article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex overlay - Attribution schedule to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule listing each partner's name, residence, legal form, percentage interest and allocated taxable share of profit/loss of the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Annex must allow each foreign partner to integrate its share in its home tax return and enables the ACD to monitor treaty eligibility of the partnership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing immediately triggers a fixed administrative fine (Ordnungsstrafe) up to EUR 25,000; ICTP-style enforcement: monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% of unpaid CIT; additional tax increase of 10% where tax is not paid by the preclusive deadline; managerial default can result in assessment by official estimate adding 25% buffer and loss of audit rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Partner-level annual CIT declaration (individual corporate general partners and limited partners resident in Luxembourg) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / MyDTD, applying the same Form 200 line logic at shareholder/partner level.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same calendar-year rule for Luxembourg-resident corporate partners; non-resident corporate partners are not required to file a Luxembourg return if the SCSp derives no Luxembourg-source income attributed to them and no permanent establishment is present in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre D - Share of partnership result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of the SCSp taxable result as computed on the partnership informational return, converted into the partner's own taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners rely on the ACD assessment and Form 200 annex rather than filing a stand-alone return; certificates of fiscal residence should be retained for treaty credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg corporate partner claiming 100% participation exemption on dividends received from the SCSp must evidence 10% holding and 12-month period (or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to non-resident partners in the partner's home jurisdiction except under local law of the partner's residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure of a Luxembourg-resident corporate partner to file its own return is subject to the same late-filing fine up to EUR 25,000 and 10% late-payment surcharge, and permits ex-officio assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Luxembourg statutory dividend WHT is 15% (LIR Art. 154). For an SCSp, cash or in-kind distributions to partners retain partnership distribution status, not dividend character, and no Luxembourg WHT is levied at the SCSp level; however, a corporate partner subsequently receiving a distribution of profits through an opaque interposed holding company would face the 15% rate unless the participation exemption (Art. 147) or Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To enjoy reduced treaty rates, the recipient partner must (1) be the beneficial owner, (2) obtain an ACD-issued Luxembourg tax residence certificate (Formulaire de résidence fiscale) and, in case of a Luxembourg intermediary, submit a declaration of beneficial ownership; (3) present the certificate to the paying agent/payer before the distribution remittance; (4) hold the 10%-ownership threshold when applicable. The ACD reviews economic substance (local management, staff, risk) before issuing the TRC; standard TRC processing takes 3-4 weeks and is renewable annually.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg levies no withholding tax on outbound royalties (domestic law: 0%). Outbound interest is likewise 0% for ordinary corporate debt; an isolated 20% WHT applies only to interest paid to Luxembourg-resident individuals on certain savings securities. In treaties, the reduced rates (commonly 5%/15% dividends; 0%-10% royalties and interest) are accessible through the same TRC/beneficial-ownership protocol; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may further reduce to 0% with 25% direct shareholding and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg TP documentation (LIR Art. 56bis, EU Transfer Pricing Documentation rules, law of 28 December 2018): Local File mandatory where intra-Group controlled transactions exceed EUR 3,000,000 in the fiscal year; Master File mandatory where the MNE group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000; a Country-by-Country Report applies when consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Documentation must be submitted to the ACD within 30 days of demand and be contemporaneous; otherwise EUR 25,000 administrative fines apply.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style ESR but enforces economic substance through the GAAR of LIR Art. 6 and 56, the ATAD anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership doctrine in DTA and EU Directives, and the OECD merciless substance requirement. A media-buying SCSp must show real operational substance: employees with actual segment pricing authority, management meetings and contract negotiation in Luxembourg, risk assumption backed by capital, and strategic budgeting; a shell SCSp whose decisions are taken in a foreign partner's office will be disregarded and its profits reallocated to the place of effective management with source-tax denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of affiliate-media-buying commissions, fabricating media placement costs, or shifting revenue to shadow foreign accounts while claiming attribution to a zero-tax partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Majoration de l'impôt: surcharge of 50%-100% of evaded CIT; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000; 10-year statute of limitation in fraud cases; CIF/SIF-based asset freezing; publication of name in the Luxembourg official gazette.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: GP partner of the SCSp personally, jointly and severally liable for partnership tax debts; liable for tribunal-restitution plus criminal imprisonment up to 5 years and travel bans; civil courts may pierce the veil under the Law of 10 August 1915 where the company is a façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / façade SCSp and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SCSp with no personnel, no physical office, no local risk control, and foreign-decision making merely to re-invoice pay-per-click media commissions with treaty-protected status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation under LIR Art. 6 and 56; refusal of residence certificate; withholding reassessment at source; ATAD hybrid rules could treat the SCSp as opaque in one state and transparent in the other, causing double non-taxation penalties and 100% reassessment; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers of the corporate GP risk being adjudged personally liable for the recaptured taxes and loss of benefit; criminal proceedings for use of artificial arrangements (abus de droit) can trigger director disqualification and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing in media arbitrage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing related advertisers or interposed digital media sub-agencies at non-arm's-length margins (e.g., 80% gross margin, unfilled inventory, unbenchmarked rev-share) without Local File/Master File, with no intercompany agreement, no functional analysis and no benchmark.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD upward adjustment of the taxpayer's taxable base under LIR Art. 56bis; interest at 0.6% per month; when documented fraud, the same 50%-100% surcharge; denial of CbC protections where the CbC report existed with inconsistent data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsibility for establishing TP documentation is personal; management can be sued for ex post re-allocation plus interest; informed non-action triggers refusal of discharge (quitus) and personal recovery in the liquidation/administration of the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering / AML-CFT violations in traffic monetisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume affiliate payouts from grey-hat media sources, using shell payment processors, mixing revenue with crypto wallets, or transacting with sanctioned/politically exposed counterparties without KYC/EDD or suspicious-transaction filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine under the Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended) up to EUR 5,000,000 per breach and up to 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions on the entity and its managers: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000; confiscation of illicit media proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officer, director and de facto manager may be prosecuted individually regardless of corporate veil; penalties include personal fines, travel bans, disqualification from managerial functions, and extradition under the European Arrest Warrant where cross-border lead-gen proceeds are laundered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report to the RCS the beneficial owner of the general partner; filing partner registry and CRS declaration with incorrect residence or with no ultimate beneficial owner identified for the press-buying shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg administrative fines per missing UBO declaration up to EUR 1,250 per month of delay for entities (or up to EUR 25,000 for repeated non-compliance); FATCA non-filing penalties under Luxembourg law; potential ban on distribution of partnership profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Office of the RCS can issue penal orders against the GP; management retains liability for organizing proper UBO registry; directors face separate sanctions for the continuity of record and failure to remedy.
